title: Seat model shape (MLLM Coder v2, IN-2)
description: Validates the three allowed shapes a seat's own config may use to route through OpenRouter's already-existing model-routing primitives (relay/runs/2026-09-14T17-25-10-314Z/deliverable.md §3), as confirmed against the real adapter behavior in test/openrouter-adapter-capabilities.test.js (IN-1). `model` is ALWAYS a plain string to src/providers.js's OpenRouter adapter - there is no 'model as array' shape in OpenRouter's own real API (docs.openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/model-fallbacks: fallback is a separate `models` array field; docs.openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/pareto-router: the Pareto Code router is invoked via a plain model-slug string plus an optional `plugins` array) - so this schema corrects the plan's own draft wording rather than encoding it literally, per IN-1's finding.

panelMaxTokens.description: Optional output cap for the panel review stage only; maxTokens still governs proposals, debate and replies.

model.description: Shape 1 (plain id): any OpenRouter model id or router slug (e.g. "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5", "openrouter/pareto-code", "openrouter/auto") as a plain string. A plain string with no `extra.models`/`extra.plugins` is byte-identical to every seat's `model` field before this schema existed - see the 'plain id, no routing' example in chains/coder-gate-v2.json.

extra.description: The adapter's existing, unmodified per-seat escape hatch (spread verbatim into the OpenRouter request body by callOpenAICompat - unchanged by this schema or by v2). Shapes 2 and 3 both live here, as siblings of `model`, never inside it.

models.description: Shape 2 (provider-array fallback): OpenRouter's own `models` field - an ordered array of fallback model ids, tried in order only on transport failure (rate limit, moderation flag, downtime), per OpenRouter's own docs. Sequencing is entirely OpenRouter-side; this adapter performs no selection or retry logic of its own (see IN-1's finding).

plugins.description: Shape 3 (routing-param route): OpenRouter's own `plugins` array, e.g. the Pareto Code Router's `[{ "id": "pareto-router", "min_coding_score": 0..1 }]`. Used together with a router slug in `model` (e.g. "openrouter/pareto-code") - the router choice itself is still a plain string in `model`, per IN-1's finding; `plugins` only configures it.
